review_scope: Frozen snapshot title and complete item body plus every receipt-listed PNG tile; audit of rendered LaTeX/TikZ, clipping, diagram semantics, and source-supported missing-diagram candidates.

diagram_candidates.title: Event-time and reset geometry for the bouncing-ball example
diagram_candidates.kind: phase-plane trajectory and event timeline (editorial candidate; uncertain)
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: The exact incoming trajectory y(t)=(1-t^2,-2t) hits q=0 at τ=1 with downward orientation; the approximate reconstruction has q-offset 1/25, reported root τhat=sqrt(26/25), and reset R(q,v)=(0,-v/2).
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Plot q versus t and v versus t (or the (q,v) phase curve), mark the exact and reported guard crossings, indicate the downward signed crossing and apply the reset to the reported event state; distinguish the exact event time from the later reported time.

diagram_candidates.title: Fold projection and two solution branches
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: The solution set of x^2-λ=0 has a simple fold at (0,0): no real solution for λ<0, one double solution at zero, and two branches x=±sqrt(λ) for λ>0; λ is not a two-sided local coordinate.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw λ=x^2 in the (λ,x) plane with both branches and the fold point, and show that projection to the λ-axis is not locally one-to-one across the fold.

diagram_candidates.title: Planar Hopf phase portrait across the parameter sign
diagram_candidates.kind: phase portrait with parameter bifurcation inset (editorial candidate; uncertain)
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: The displayed planar cubic field has polar equations rdot=μr-r^3 and θdot=1; for μ>0 the nonzero radial equilibrium is r=sqrt(μ), with negative radial derivative, yielding a stable periodic orbit of period 2π.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show the origin and concentric cycle r=sqrt(μ) for μ>0, radial arrows pointing toward the cycle, counterclockwise angular orientation from θdot=1, and optionally the cycle-radius branch versus μ. Do not depict a cycle for μ≤0.

diagram_candidates.title: Two-state gate transition graph with column generator convention
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: The off-to-on rate is α and on-to-off rate is β; for the column probability vector (p_off,p_on)^T the generator is Q=[[-α,β],[α,-β]], with each source state indexed by a column.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw nodes off/on, directed arrows off→on labelled α and on→off labelled β, and beside it the displayed column generator with column sums zero; indicate the initial off state and p_on(t)=α(1−e^(−(α+β)t))/(α+β) when α+β>0.

diagram_candidates.title: Projection onto a convex set and outward normal correction
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: For p=P_C(y), p lies in C and y−p lies in the outward normal cone N_C(p); projection Euler maps x_k to P_C(x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)) and linearly interpolates consecutive projected nodes.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Use a simple closed convex planar set as an explicitly illustrative special case; mark trial point y, nearest point p, segment y−p perpendicular to a smooth boundary where applicable, and outward normal cone at p. A separate small step sketch can show x_k+h f projected back to C as x_(k+1), with the affine segment. Do not imply smoothness or uniqueness beyond the convex-projection statement.

diagram_candidates.title: Event-aligned error propagation through mode segments and resets
diagram_candidates.kind: hybrid time-line with mode-segment state tracks (editorial candidate; uncertain)
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: Exact event times τ_j precede reported upper-box times τhat_j; compare paths at the reported time in the outgoing mode, propagate aligned start discrepancy E_j through each mode segment and reset to E_(j+1), with lag Δ_(j+1)<δ/3 preserving event order.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw exact and reported trajectories with labeled mode segments, exact event τ_j, later reported event τhat_j, guard bracket/lag, reset jump, and aligned outgoing comparison at τhat_j. Show E_j entering the segment, D_j incoming error, and E_(j+1) after reset. Make explicit that no same-clock state error is claimed between the exact jump and the later reported jump.

diagram_candidates.title: Fine/coarse Poisson tau-leap coupling over two half intervals
diagram_candidates.kind: coupling timeline with shared and residual count streams (editorial candidate; uncertain)
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: Each fine step h is paired with a coarse step 2h on two half intervals; each channel uses a shared min-intensity Poisson count plus fine/coarse positive-part residual counts, the fine state updates between halves, and coarse counts are accumulated at the coarse starting state.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw one coarse interval split into two fine half-intervals; above/below it track fine state updates versus the held coarse state. For each channel mark the shared count mean h min(a_j(x),a_j(z)) and the two residual means, then show the two coarse count vectors accumulated into one coarse leap.

diagram_candidates.title: Age-time upwind mesh and renewal inflow boundary
diagram_candidates.source_supported_claim: The finite-volume scheme uses age/time grids with transport-plus-loss CFL, cellwise constant reconstructions, newborn mass supplied at the renewal boundary, and an absorbing right cutoff; the theorem gives L1 convergence without requiring initial-trace/birth-rate compatibility.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw age a horizontally and time t vertically, transport characteristics moving with slope da/dt=1, the age-zero renewal inflow, cell fluxes on the upwind grid, and the cutoff outflow. Mark that the initial trace may mismatch the birth boundary at (a,t)=(0,0), so the drawing does not suggest compatibility or a Taylor error rate.
